Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• Likely acute asthma exacerbation, precipitated by viral infection or seasonal allergens—consistent with history of asthma, atopy, and sudden 2–3-day deterioration (DDx “High” likelihood).  
• Viral upper/lower respiratory tract infection or acute bronchitis may be contributing (DDx “Medium” likelihood).  
• Allergic (pollen-induced) flare also possible given hay fever/eczema background (DDx “Medium” likelihood).  
No conflicting information between transcript and DDx noted.

Management Plan
- Increase salbutamol inhaler use to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours via spacer (spacer to be supplied).  
- Prescribe spacer and peak-flow meter; pharmacist to demonstrate correct technique.  
- Record peak-flow values morning and evening for one week; arrange follow-up review in one week to evaluate need for additional controller therapy.  
- Start regular over-the-counter antihistamine for hay fever symptoms (specific agent/dose not documented).  
- Safety-net advice: seek urgent review if temperature rises, wheeze worsens, or breathlessness increases.
